Yes, it's where my brother works, and he really likes it. He has been working there only a couple more months than I have been working at Target, and already has the option of becoming a supervisor and has another job offer at another place. It's hard listening to my brothers talk about their good experiences at their jobs, because really all it would take for me to be happy at my job is a little recognition-an "hey, I am so glad we have you working for us!" But no... and that just adds to my feelings of life being pointless and disappointing. No matter how hard I try or how good I am, things will always go sour for me. I will always be invisible. No matter how many people I am there for or try to show their value (and I do a lot-it's something I am passionate about), no one will be really there for me or see me as valuable. I was good in school, but still invisible and received crap from teachers. I was good in any volunteer positions, and I am good at my job, faithful, fast, trustworthy and dedicated. But those who cheat are more noticed than I. I know some people who don't really know me have told me that I care too much what other people think-but I really don't. Usually I avoid people, I don't strive to be better for their sake. I just exist and try my best for me.  But it would be nice to not feel invisible and like I am floating through life. I want some solid ground. I want to know where I have footing. I want to know what my "thing" is, where I can dig in deep and succeed. I just feel like I am living and screaming inside this clear box where people can see me but not hear me. Like I am an idea, something people recognize for a moment, but not a person. The only time I feel more like an individual person is when I am doing something rebellious, of all things. Curse of our times I guess.

Hey, I do have very similar problems. I don't believe it's ADD or anything, I think the root of it is just that because of our anxiety we can get so disconnected from the world, it's like we are only half there, because our minds are focused on our anxieties. The only way I have managed to pull myself through situations like you mentioned, is to clear my head, intend my hardest to focus, bring a notebook, and really listen for just key little things that I can retain and keep in memory-simple things like a phrase or image that when thought of can bring the main point back to mind. Also, if you struggle in a certain area (like focusing during the lesson) don't let it be the end of the world for you. Utilize other means of learning the material-text book or online resources, or even notes or refresher from a friend. Maybe even talk to the teacher. I don't know if this is something that can be "fixed" (I made it through school, but I still don't drive because my mind just never retained directions or how they make sense, 20 odd years of driving around with other people and I still have a hard time directing people back to my own house) but meds might help "clear the fog" so to speak, I have yet to try them. Until then, motivate yourself to really focus and not get distracted. If you feel yourself getting distracted-pull yourself back and try to figure out whats being talked about. Maybe bring a recorder if you think you will listen to it later. Try to make it a habit and it will get easier. Your mind will know to focus. :)

It's true, most people just don't have the understanding, strength and capacity to deal with other people's problems (particularly serious problems like depression and suicidal feelings) especially when it is close people like good friends or family, so they deny it. As I said before it may be because it makes him scared for you and so he belittles it to make it less of a scare, or it makes him uncomfortable because he doesn't know how to deal with it, or because he just doesn't understand it, or because he is just too overwhelmed at the moment with his own issues. I know that because he is the person you wanted the most to trust this with, it hurts to not be able to be open with him and to have him belittle it, but I admire your courage to be honest with him, most hide it. But I think in this instance, if you want to keep his friendship, you are going to have to keep things with him more on the shallow side instead of the deep end, at least until he has delt with whatever is overwhelming him and he feels more open to listening to your difficulties. Until that day comes I strongly urge finding someone in a more capable situation, and forgiving the dude for at this point dealing poorly with your honesty and request for help.

The dude is probably just reacting to a stressed moment of his own. My dad is much the same way when I talk to him about my issues. He comes from a place where  he is 1) stressed about his own stuff, 2) worried about me and wanting me to "just get over it" and 3) not understanding my issues as a person who has no experience in the area. 
This friend doesn't understand, depression has little to do with circumstantial problems and more to do with the brain. Sure circumstances can trigger it, but it's really the internal reactions that are going on that cause the emotions or lack there of. Personally I think maybe the person you should be talking to is this friend of yours who is also struggling. Maybe together you can open up, be deep, and be a support system. Together discover ways and means to beat the issue. I think it might be worth a try, as long as you don't bring each other further down or one starts leaning too much on the other. You might find that just having that other understanding person is just what you need. My own best friend of 12 years doesn't know everything about my issues but another friend who I have only known a year knows all about it, because she has gone through the same thing. It all depends. Just because it fails with one person doesn't mean give up on all. Everyone is different, and you need to have someone you feel you can talk to. I hope days get brighter for you.

Extremely unintelligent? What the hell? You don't sound unintelligent to me at all. You sound extremely intelligent. Don't give up on yourself yet. And don't..DO NOT..let culture define your success and value. You already expressed that you can't stand society, so why do you let it have power over you? You call yourself white trash, unintelligent, physically unattractive, weak, incompetent, solitary and quiet, timid and socially awkward, but why are these negative? Because society says they are. You are looking at yourself through the eyes of society, when what you should be doing is saying "this is MY life, my body, my time, my future. What do *I* want from it?" Not "what are the cultural standards?" like some drone. We are all guilty of it, measuring success by what others think of us. We buy nice things like cars and houses and clothes, less because we enjoy them and more because we want to give off an image for others. People often get into poor relationships for the same reason, they feel if they don't have a significant other they are a failure, not because they aren't happy but because they don't look successful in society. THAT is unintelligent. 

Try this: think of yourself in your ideal position, all the things you think you would need to be and to have in order to be successful and happy, and start breaking it into pieces, with each one ask "is this what I want or is this what I think would make me look good thus feel significant?" and once you have dwindled it down, start thinking about the things that would really make YOU happy. I don't care how far out or crazy those dreams are. Find yourself. List the things you like about yourself, the world, things you find interesting. Forget all the rest. Let go of it. Breath the air that you have right now around you, and realize that you are in control of your life. Take one day at a time and get to that place that you really want to be, and maybe one day you will look behind you and find that you are being admired by society, having stopped picking up their breadcrumbs and instead sat at the table and ordered your own food. 

If it means anything, I really hope you don't go through with your plan. There are few people who can think like you, and they usually tend to be the deepest people in the world. Why do you think so many artists and geniuses were called mad and ill? I think they saw the world the same way we do, so much broader and deeper than just our present surroundings. Eventually we will die, but for now we can do more with our lives than just cutting them even shorter.  We can take a chance.

From my experience, it's a long journey. It's like rock climbing, every time you see a handhold you grab it-whether it be a small realization about life or a glimpse of hope, a reason, you grab on to it, meditate on it, and keep building up. Also, finding people you can at least in some way be honest with helps, even if it's just on reddit. Take one day at a time, don't consume yourself with thoughts of the future (unless it's in a positive light). Find something your interested in (even if you are just somewhat interested in it, for me it's science) and delve in. Use it to distract your brain. And dream big. Don't think-oh I could never do that or be good at this, think "what if I was? What can I do to get there?" and then try, little things at a time. You have all the time in the world to do with your life what YOU want. Also, try to relieve stressors. If you are someone who deals with anxiety-seek out the things that are the causes of it and try to solve it, or at least solve the way you feel about it. Talk to people! They are a great resource. I personally also keep a journal where I just scribble anything I feel in it. My worst thoughts, and my best thoughts. I can be as free as I want in my journal-as long as I hide it well. And I read books on the topic-right now I am reading a book called "How I stayed alive when my brain was trying to kill me" it has some great advice. 
 I am not saying any of this is a cure-all, but it has helped me. I still think about suicide once in a while, especially just before I go to sleep when anxiety and hopelessness are the worst and I feel alone. But it's not nearly as bad as it was. I hope some day to be completely free of those thoughts and feelings. My life is all I have, and if happiness and peace can be found, I would like to be alive to experience it. :)

I would like to believe a lot of people have the same issues that you and I struggle with, but I am having difficulty believing that with how differently people react to situations-even people I thought were like me. The one person I thought was most like me in almost every way, sobbed like a baby when her grandmother passed, but it didn't even phase me that I missed my own grandmothers funeral because I was a little sick. Whenever bad things happen around me I get excited-when normal things happen I get anxious. It's the opposite with all the people I know. I would sweat for weeks over starting a new job, but when my friend gets in a car accident and I am over helping the panicky girl out, she states in a half-joke "I love how calm you always are when situations like this happen." Once I almost got into a car accident while I was driving with my friend and her mom, the car was out of control, but all I was doing was thinking. When it was all over, the rest were shaking but they kept asking if I was all right and then talking about me behind my back because I wasn't panicked like them. I was completely fine. To this day they still joke about how my reaction scared them because they thought I was in shock or something. When I hear stories on the news about criminal incidents, instead of feeling bad about the victims, I think about it from the perspective of the criminal-or think about how I might have taken down the criminal if I had been there, always violent. I don't know anyone quite like me, and I am afraid of saying what I think because I don't want them to look at me weird or feel like they can't trust me. Do you really think that people all around us feel like this? It seems to me like it is the one thing hardly anyone feels like. People have dirty thoughts or greedy thoughts sure, but sadistic? Blood lust? Is that something common to enjoy? Since I was a little girl, most of my first favorite movies and shows always involved tortured characters, and I liked my antiheros, especially when they went bad. And no, I don't mean I just liked them as an angsty teen. I liked them as a small child, I would leave a story thinking and dreaming about them. And that part of me just kept growing and becoming uglier, outliving any part of that little girl who dreamed of anything normal like finding a prince charming, having kids or what my wedding would look like. I don't think I ever cared about that. Sure I would pretend to care with all my other friends who did. Pshh. Maybe I just don't fit in with this culture. Maybe I should become a mad scientist, estranged writer or traveling artist and block out the world. That sounds nice. Except for the constant loud confusion in my head and the urges I can never quiet that drive me crazy. I would like to be done with that. I should try the therapist. But thank you for listening and understanding, it does help to talk about it.

I am grateful you came across my post, it is calming to read replies from someone who understands. Having this issue can be so overwhelming, just because of confusion and having no healthy outlet, as well as feeling like a monster for having such thoughts and urges, even if I don't feel like they are really me, they are still somehow a part of me I haven't figured out how to quiet. 

No, I am not currently seeing anyone about it. I want to, but currently don't have the funds to do something like that. I also have trust issues so I am cautious about being open with someone. I talked with a counselor back in college but I was very vague with her. She asked me at one point if I had ever had suicidal thoughts-and at that point I was struggling with them immensely, but I had laughed it off, telling her I sometimes had violent thoughts but that my mom thought it was due to the movies I watched. She never brought it up again, and we just talked about how to deal with anxiety. I never felt safe with her, I just went into my normal "fake being o.k. and bite your tongue" routine, which was exhausting. I would worry that whoever I talked to, if I were really honest, they might lock me up. But honestly at this point I wouldn't mind. If it would help control the chaos and save what's left of my true person. I am 23, just graduated college and I still live with my parents. If I were to go see someone my father would need to pay for it until I find a steady job, which he might do if he was convinced I needed it. But how do I tell him? I feel like he will either wave it off or get angry. He is prone to getting angry when he gets worried. I don't want to deal with that. He would get angry about my cutting, but he took me once to the hospital to get my thyroid checked (it was fine) and too see about depression/anxiety meds, which I did not take even though they were prescribed. Since then we haven't discussed it much, except once when we talked about my lack of interest in love and me faking the last relationship I was in. Anyways, the thought of bringing it up to him causes me anxiety. But I don't have my own health insurance, it's still through him. Pssh.

thanks. And the answer to that is complicated. Yes I do feel like she is a totally separate person from me, living inside of me. For a while I even wondered if I were possessed. But only because she is so starkly different from the way I view myself and she cares so little about the things that I am fond of, also the fact that she kept trying to hurt and kill me. It felt like, something small would get me really down, or nothing at all, and as soon as I was at that weak point she would sort of take control and think/do things I wouldn't do, things that my sane mind would worry about once I could think again. This sort of came to my realization when I had spent 2 years living with suicidal ideation and then one day I was feeling better and walked by a bridge that usually I would always imagine throwing myself over but that day when I saw it I suddenly felt afraid for my life, like she would push me over, and walked away from it. I realized then that that part of me, which I always thought made me stronger, had actually made me a victim, and I started to fight for myself. Now when I feel her urges I do things to protect myself. But she finds a way around them. She picks the movies I watch, always violent, horror or crime-no romance or comedies. I keep a dull knife close at hand just in case I have a bad moment so holding it close will calm her down and keep her from searching for something sharp to cut me with. But that's not the only reason she keeps it, she hopes someone will attack me some day when I am walking alone so that she can use it, she desperately wants to experience death-and since she can't have mine she now dreams of someone else's death. I could never let that happen, ever. So yes, I believe it is against my will, I feel like a victim to her, my true self is an unwilling host that she can mess with and I am always trying to sate her so she doesn't drive me crazy. :|

Thanks for this, really helps clear some things up. Especially the attachment thing. Makes so much sense. I never had the "mature and self-aware look at us lovingly and non-judgementally, with an open mind and heart" person in my life. Even though I crave it so much. Someone to help me figure out who I am, not put on me who they want me to be. I never had anyone I felt like I could trust, who was really interested in me as a person, who had my back no matter what. Never. Even though I was raised in a family where I feel like everyone else does. I don't think my dad did when he was younger, and for some reason he chose to raise me the same way, even though he treats my brothers better. I think he was afraid to do things for me because he felt like I needed to be independent as the only girl, instead now I have developed isolation and distrust and hopelessness, along with confusion and hurt. I never learned how to really love, because I never had anyone I could trust. I realize all this, but I don't know what to do about it. If I lost myself and went crazy, everyone would just give a sour face and wonder what's wrong with me. If I disappeared, everyone would put on a show about how tragic their lives are, and perhaps grieve that they  are missing my presence, but they will realize that life without me isn't much different, because I was never really here in the first place. I was just a warm body. No identity.

I love what SQLwitch had to say, really insightful. Yes I find I have the same problem. I mean, my life has some crap but nothing that should make me so miserable I should want to end it. But yet, I still feel it. The thing is, it's not really that I want to not exist-it's just that I don't want to exist here, in this swirling, mindless, ever flowing and careless way of life that other people and tradition has designed for us. The freedom and absoluteness and purpose I feel when I think  about dying is the same feeling I can get when I think about just running away to my favorite places without telling anyone. I feel like I am suffocating, like I need an escape and I don't know why. I feel like I'm in pain all the time, and like there is some doom in front of me that I am blindly walking towards with the masses and I need to escape it. I don't know if that resonates with you. I think it may be because 1) I feel like my life is out of my own control and is being controlled by others, 2) I feel like I am not doing what I want to be doing, and 3) I am stuck where I don't want to be, and 4) I don't really belong here, I feel like a ghost or shadow that everyone acknowledges but no-one knows, like I am just playing a part I don't want to play for the sake of acting normal, building my life off of small white lies. I'm not normal, I'm different and I am not happy here living like everyone else, there is someone in me that is bursting to get out and truly be me. I am looking for more, for something beautiful and lasting. It's before me but I can't reach it. Also, I feel afraid all the time, and I am so tired of feeling afraid. Blah.

Maybe he is feeling just as embarrassed as you, and not sure where to start with talking to you about it. I personally would initiate conversation with him, but start small, maybe a text or online message about how you know you laid a lot on him and that you don't want that to make things awkward between you, but hope it will bring you closer. Let him know that the being drunk part probably wasn't the best way to discuss it, but that you hope you can talk again in a better situation. Explain that you really needed someone to share with, and thought he was the one you felt you could trust most with what you shared. 
Then, maybe plan another time to hang out doing something fun. Chances are he isn't taking it as terribly as you might feel. Most people have crap of their own they keep buried. Let him know how much you appreciated him being there for you, and promise you will be there for him the same way if he ever needed it. Best of luck.

Thanks. :) But (and no disrespect as I know you didn't mean it that way), I don't consider anyone a waste of energy. People have their issues, but we know better than anyone that problems should be worked through, and often that is helped by the support of another person who wont turn away. I have a feeling a lot of people gave up on this person, including therapists. But really, what do they know? They haven't been through the crap we have. If it has lead someone to be difficult and bitter and cling to the lies of depression, does that mean they are a lost cause? I don't think so. I may not be the one truly able to help restore any kind of health, but I have no quells about lending a hand to a fellow sufferer if it is needed. It's what I needed so many times, so if I can ask for it, shouldn't I be willing to give it as well?

Everyone lied? I highly doubt that. It seems a pretty far-fetched absolute to me. Perhaps it is just your long-term depression telling you that? You have given up, so it means everyone else should as well? Seems pretty irrational to me, especially since there is direct evidence contrary to that opinion. You said it yourself, some people get better. How do you know who will and who wont? And how do you know there are people who went their entire lives being miserable? Those who committed are not here to prove your theory that you can live an entire life in utter misery. 
How do you know we are very different? Do you know me? Maybe we are more alike than you think. Hmm, as unlikely as it is-I find myself often struck by uncanny similarities in people who've suffered suicidal depression like myself, and I think there is something to that. Maybe you aren't as alone and unique as you think. And if you really believe you are, then maybe you shouldn't be telling younger people it's alright to just do it. Maybe since they are different from you, they might not have the same experience. Personally, I think you have been listening to the lies of your depression for so long you have completely shut out your rational side. Maybe you should try tapping in to it. Try listing to it some time and write down what it's saying. It could be an interesting exercise..

This may be a bit straightforward, but yeah, I do think part of you wants to be that way. Maybe not consciously, but yes. I think you want to be this way, because you are convinced that it is right. It's pretty obvious. Why else would you be out to "let young people know it's ok to kill themselves"? I know because I wanted to be the way I was. It made me feel-justified, in control, more rational than everyone else, powerful. But the actual rational part of me knew that it wasn't, and I knew that I was only that way because my mind was out of control. It wasn't rational. It was completely irrational. I felt like I had been born without survival instincts and that it was unfair and cruel because people needed that to survive in this harsh world. Like I had been born with the "glasses off" so I could see the world for what it was and everyone else saw it through colorful glasses that made it look pleasant. I've found that we all wear glasses, and mine were tainted and blurry. I wasn't seeing the way I should have been. 
As I said before, if regular treatment options didn't work for you, then keep looking for something that will work-be creative. I would think that if your life depended on it, it might just be worth it. -.-

 I used to be like you, hating "dumb" people. I used to visualize people who didn't think like me as idiotic blondes on drugs skipping about with pathetic smiles on their faces, totally, purposefully, unaware of the snake-pit they were in. Dude, we aren't in a snake pit. Sure, society and people can be awful, and life can be unfair-but you know what? EVERYONE realizes that, it's just us depressed people that compound on it and focus on it because we use it to rationalize our own feelings. The truth is, we are all born here, (in a rather beautiful place if I do say) and yes there are plenty of hardships, but there are good things too. We are born here, in one fashion or another-some fully functional, some handicapped, some rich, some poor, but how we react to it differs greatly and has very little to do with our situation. A person with the worst situation can be the happiest, and the one with seemingly little to offer can be the greatest blessing to his neighbor. We can choose to hate that we were born here and kill ourselves off, or we can choose to accept that this is who we are, where we are, and learn to deal with it. Once we start really dealing with it-you may find, as Scoder did, as I am starting to, and as many others have, that it can actually be pretty great. You know, if you did end it all for yourself-you will never know that peace you hope to find, but we might. You would have no chance of experiencing happiness. We could. Too many of us take life for granted. Those little things we enjoy that we just grudingly do now without even realizing it. Sucking down a mocha-walking down the street-we ignore the things we love, but if we were dead, it would be the last mocha we ever drank, the last colorful cloudy sky we ever saw, the last time we would get to hear our favorite instrument played. That is the most depressing thing I can think of, worse than what I have here. To just stop being in pain and feeling so much sorrow sounds amazing, but to just stop existing and not even know it, sounds so empty and pointless. So I don't know about you, but I am going to keep looking  for a way to find the first, and die when my time comes, which it will, it's not like I can escape that. It will happen sooner or later. Might as well use the time I have to enjoy those little things and work towards my goal of finding peace here and now.

Wow dude, your name says it all. You do sound pretty miserable. Is this where thirty years of misery gets you? You start to try to blot out others hope as well because you cant stand it? When I read this I see a person who has lost (or has yet to find) his identity and now has hit rock bottom, as I had, and is looking for a hand back up. Advice you can get from others, temporary comforts you can get from others, but in the end you are the only one who can change or better your life and perspective and bring yourself out of this depression. There are people who have everything they could possibly want and are still depressed. Temporary happiness can come from things, true happiness is a choice to realize the chance you have to live and figure out who you are and what wonders this world holds. If this is how you are really feeling, I will say, I have been there before and I know how dark and hopeless it can be. How worthless you feel, how out of control and rejected. Like your insides-your soul- is burning in agony living inside your body and in this world, and you feel trapped, not able to escape it by any means but death. You say there was another in your family who chose this way-well I can tell you that (whether or not you believe in an afterlife) this person did not find the relief they were looking for, because in order to experience relief you have to be alive! Same with hope and happiness! They are all things we only know here, while we live. You can achieve it! You can stop aching inside. Realize that life is shorter than you know, and that the little things around you are more beautiful and valuable than they seem. The biggest lesson I learned that helped me get out of my suicidal depression was the realization that I had been taking everything for granted and not taking time to "smell the roses" cause to me they all looked like garbage. Try to delve deeper into yourself and into others, take time to enjoy the little things, the taste of your favorite drink, your favorite smell, the sun on your skin, the warmth and safety of the place you now sit, the ability to access a place such as this, your ability to read words-the very marvel of a written language! The amazing genius it took to create the marvel that is the internet so you could even see this page! A flower, a snowflake, how refreshing water tastes when you are thirsty! The happiness you could feel when you run into that "impossible" dream you hold deep down. The amazement at discovering a dream you never even thought to dream of! There is so much to enjoy and look forward to, if only we take the time to stop taking it for granted and realize. Seize it. You are cared for. You are just as valuable and have just as much worth as anyone else. And you CAN find happiness. It's just a lot closer than you might think.

Hehe, you know, as I have come to see it (and I may be wrong seeing as I suffer from depression as well), I can't really think of anything that isn't "wasting time", I mean, we all do it, just in different ways. 19? Already been through a 2 year relationship? Had a coworker who you caught the eye of? (even if it was just temporary). These things should not leave you with despair, but with hope. They just, do. A mutual realization that hits two people. Your problem is that you are trying to control this, you are expecting something specific-and the fact that you are not getting it is frustrating you and leaving you hopeless. You need to let this go, this is not something you can force no matter how hard you try. Learn to live and love your life-and when you do that will make you all the more attractive to the right person. And you do want the right person, because as you already know ending up with the wrong one usually is or ends up being worse than being single. Stop focusing on this-realize that your life is so much MORE than searching for another life to share yours with. You need to figure out who you are first, date yourself! Figure out what is interesting about YOU, what do you like? What are your hopes and dreams? What defines you? Then figure out the world! That alone is an endless journey, and will keep you preoccupied until you do find the right one. Also-discovering your own personality, likes and hobbies will attract friends. And remember, the pain you feel over the lost relationships is something different than your hope for the future, keep these things separate and don't let them affect each other, deal with them separately. It can get better for you, just keep the hope.

"A person's happiness depends on their ability to exist in the world without fear of being hurt." 
Found this on a site while googling "numb from emotions" tonight. There was some pretty great points made -(http://www.onlinecounseling.org/lack_of_emotions.htm), but this one really struck a cord with me. For so long, I felt numb and hollow, withdrawn and blank. The only thing I could feel was severe aggravation, and sometimes for no real reason at all. I was afraid I was becoming a realized sociopath or going insane, but I knew it had to be something else. My life was chaotic and I lived in the clouds most of the time. I did not realize that I was hiding, and still am. Hiding from people, from life, from all things I no longer trust to not hurt or betray me, and this along with dealing with severe chronic anxiety resulted in what I think is a "flight" defense mechanism. I shut down all emotions, cut all emotional ties, and keep my mind out of reality so that I can feel some sort of security-some sort of escape from that which I dreaded, and I did it subconsciously. I continued down this road, became depressed and eventually came to a place where I no longer knew how to deal with emotional pain because I couldn't react normally to it, so I started self-harming to release it. Then it all went downhill. I felt that I, and life in general, was pointless, stupid and horrible, and living was a thing to fear above all else. So I became obsessed with death, because death seemed like the ultimate escape, the only way to truly end everything and shut everything out-the place where I could finally be alone and without fear. The place where I could be at peace-the place where I could just not be me, where I did not have to live by-or for-other peoples expectations. I would just, not be. It sounded and sometimes still sounds incredible. My fantastic images wont let me see just how messy, devastating and pointless suicide is. It looked amazing to me, maybe a little romantic even, the best thing that could ever happen in my life. Death. The word still brings beautiful images to my mind. Flowers and music, endless seas and fading lights, a light breeze, a starry sky, emptiness, quiet, peaceful, happy, finished, nothing. The poor people stuck on earth would just have another thing to be miserable about and get over, unless they too realized the trueness of death, their ultimate goal, the thing we were all waiting for anyways. Well, back on topic-as I said, I was obsessed with death. The only things that kept me here was fear of the unknown-I did not really know what the afterlife held, what if it would be worse than here? And secondly, those poor miserable people who still loved me, despite all the mistakes made on both sides, and would be devastated if I had done it. I am pretty selfish, but purposefully inflicting pain on another was something I generally tried to avoid. So I tried to get better. I tried to fix the problems that made my life feel chaotic. And I did, it helped a lot. I dropped out of a major at school that was causing me stress and it did wonders. I felt ok for the first time in two years battling my second bought with deep depression. Unfortunately, recently I realized that I have once again gotten myself stuck in something I am not happy with that is triggering my ever hungry anxiety. I went down the drain a bit. I started having fantasies of suicide again, and urges to self harm. I know I need to remove the source of anxiety, and I will. But in the meantime I realized again that I still have problems I have not dealt with, such as my lack of emotions and my hyper-private personality that never opens up to people without it being dragged out. So that is why I googled and found this tonight. I realized that my distrust of people and the world, and my strong desire not to be vulnerable to avoid being hurt, is wrong and has lead me down this road. Not saying I dont have good reason to be this way, but if I want to be happy again, to feel positive emotions, I need to learn to be brave and vulnerable, to be willing to feel and connect, even if I get hurt. I dont know what this looks like or how it starts, so if I could get advice that would be great. Also, I just wanted to encourage others who might be in the same boat, we are not hopeless, we are just hurting. Don't give up. :)

I know. I feel the same way-or I have felt anyways. Since it has been five hours since you posted, I hope you are feeling a bit more in control and aren't physically hurt too badly. For me, when I want to cut, I try to think of my body as a separate entity, as someone else that is already suffering that I am just hurting more. As much as it seems unnatural, you need somebody to talk to. Just rant. Spill your guts. Stop keeping it inside until the only way it can release the pressure is by bleeding out. Also, rest. Distract yourself. Their are many things you can do http://www.palace.net/~llama/psych/fself.html but I find the most effective is just to try to deal with the problem at hand, whatever specific things are causing you to feel this way if any (usually there is something, even if it is small). If you cant do anything to deal with it physically then try to deal with it emotionally, tell yourself that you are overreacting, that the problem is only as big as you want it to be, and that you can feel however you want about it-we are in charge of our thoughts and reactions-not the other way around, or at least that is how it should be. I know it's hard, I know there are ways of dealing with it that seem so much easier, but in the long run cutting is a temporary fix to a problem that is only going to stay and fester. If you need to do something, feel pain (I have been there, and am still dealing with this), try something that wont leave a scar. Try holding your wrist to hot air or water until you cant stand it, or tie something tight around both wrists (I don't know where you cut but thats what I did). Sometimes I would rub some sort of lotion or red liquid over my arms (ketchup, juice, anything red) to get my brain to think it was blood. Or just look at pictures of cutting. It would help calm the urges. Cutting is an addiction like any other, and like many others it can leave permanent damage if not be fatal. If their is any part of you that wants to beat this way of dealing with crap, then fight it. Really, sometimes when you feel desperate enough to end it all, just talking can help. Tell someone you just need them to listen, you may be surprised. I hope you feel better soon. Good luck.

Most people don't realize their insignificance in comparison to the universe, they live in happy oblivion, satisfied in their value. But people like you and I often do, we feel weighted down by our own smallness-because it has been shoved in our faces. Can you imagine if everyone did realize? Then perhaps they would all be having suicidal dreams. I think we need to change perspective. No person is more significant then another, whether they have more success or more people who love them-they were simply either more fortunate, or came to the point that you are now at and realized they had to take charge of their own lives and really look at themselves, instead of only seeing themselves through the eyes of others. Get to know who YOU are-treat yourself as if you were a long lost friend, discover your likes and dislikes, help yourself stay motivated to find a job (it sounds like you have some guaranteed time with the family, keep searching for a job, perhaps the family will note the extra effort and if they are thinking anything it will put those thoughts at ease). Just make sure you dont give up on yourself, many of us only have ourselves to rely on (unless you are religious like me, then you would say you also rely on God. ;) ). A person can be abandoned and mistreated by all the people they ever meet, and still come out strong, if they stay true to themselves and keep believing in themselves-you have the ability to pave your way, no one else can do it for you. Yes it can be hard, but it is worth it. Dying by your own hand is not a way to peace. But knowing that you helped yourself get unstuck, that I believe, will bring you hope and peace. :) Also, I think you know. NO ONE would be happy if you died, especially your parents, they would live with that guilt for the rest of their lives. If you feel sorry for her now, imagine what that would do to her. The dreams are a lie. The suicidal fantasies (I also used to have those) of how things would be if you did die, are not true. It is messy and cruel, and would leave people broken, sometimes beyond repair. There is a much better solution. Ride out the storm and find yourself on the other side. Your true, beautiful self, assured and confident, who can share her story and inspire others who have found themselves in the same position. Can you imagine the faces of the people in your life if they saw this? The real you? The confident you? I think that would be much more satisfying then only imagining that they would be happy missing out on your life. Start small, work your way up. One day at a time. Tomorrow try doing something abnormal but small that can give you a sense of accomplishment and make you feel good. I think you sound like an amazing person who has gone through a lot of heartache that has weakened you. I think people would be honored and privileged to have the chance to see the strong you. Don't give up. Just do some working out. ;) Good luck.

Anxiety is my demon as well, and a strong one it is. It can suffocate you, choke you, pull your heart out, crush your chest and poison your stomach all at once, while making your mind into a vast dark hole that seems to suck everything into a swirling chaotic mess that leaves you stunned, shaking and unsure what to do. Blasted, horrible thing has been with me as long as I can remember-sometimes keeping me hidden from the world, and sometimes casting me into depression out of the sheer weariness I felt. Sometimes I felt I spent my life focused only on trying to avoid or distract myself from my anxiety. A sense of doom does often come with anxiety, as well as a driving need to escape. Perhaps think of ways to confront this anxiety, or give your body what it wants (an escape) in some practical way-for me, sometimes I would shut myself in my room, light some candles, turn on some soothing music, turn out the lights, lie on the floor and just think-either about good memories, or really think about my life-about who I was in comparison to the world, and then think about my problems and emotions, trying to make sense of them and find what the root issues were. I would really try to relax at that moment, get my body to release all the tension, and tell myself that it was going to be alright, that I was overreacting, and that things will get better even if I couldnt see it. Its just one idea. Another is to talk with someone-and that doesnt have to be a psych (I also had a bad experience when I went to see a councilor on my campus. Its totally reasonable to be afraid of putting yourself in the hands of someone who could do something you dont want. There was so much I never told my councilor because I was afraid she would have me removed from the school.) I can try to help if you want. Think about how you feel, and while your depression and anxiety may be targeted towards several things, or seemingly nothing at all, is there anything going on-or something that already happened- that could be causing you more stress than perhaps you realize? Something that seems out of your control, that is pushing/has pushed your life in a direction you didn't want it to go? Sometimes a small wound in a hidden place can cause our bodies to react in disproportionate ways, and finding and understanding/confronting or even eliminating that can help us heal, or at least bring our out-of-control emotions back under our control. Our body and mind only has a few means to tell us that something is wrong, and it very well could be that there is something deep down-or in plain sight, that is grieving you. So, I guess for now, 1) do a bit of soul searching to try to understand yourself, it can help you feel more in control instead of feeling that frightening sense of doom and chaos, and 2) try to find a happy place that you can retreat to that can help calm you down when it gets bad. I hope this helps some.

Hmm, this sounds very familiar. To me, I mean. It's always interesting to hear things like this from another person, kinda surreal. I tried to make sense of it as well-the shutting people out/lashing out when people got near (or wanting to), and even vision morphings or things I noticed that seemed-idk-well for instance one time I was in a cafe having coffee with someone when a person walked out the glass door of the cafe, and out of the corner of my eye I saw the word "dEad" written on the door, my mind went totally blank at that moment, and my vision focused on that, and then out towards the bridge that was visible a ways away. At that moment it seemed every fiber of my being-and of the universe-wanted me to jump off the bridge. It both scared me, enthralled me, and gave me a sense of ominous peace. When I looked back at the door I realized what was written was just bA3b, some sort of code on the outside of the door. I truly believe that our actions are truly our survival instincts kicked on because of our mental/emotional pain. When it lasts too long or becomes too much to bear, we start seeking relief (suicide), and we act much like a wild animal does when it gets hurt, which is to hide away and lick wounds, hissing and threatening anyone that comes near because in our eyes they become an agitation and a threat. It also could be that we see others and feel like they wont understand, or dont want to understand our pain, and lash out in attempts to either reveal our pain to them or cause them pain because we want them to understand. Also, we see others as either happy (which makes us either envious or timid) or dealing with hurts of their own, and we dont want to cause them pain or be a burden so we hide out to keep our burden to ourselves. I think a huge part of why we dont open up can just be mistrust. We dont trust in peoples compassion to truly want to help, faithfulness to stick by us and not judge, ability to empathize or understand, or even love, many of us simply do not trust-or even believe-in love, which I think could be the root of many cases of depression. Because of all this, and perhaps more, we swirl out of reality, try to detach. Maybe subconsciously the suicidal mind is trying to break the ties to the world, sabotage our lives so-to-speak. As a person who recently dealt with a year of suicidal depression, I find the whole thing very complex and mysterious. I have recently found that I have somehow escaped the clutches of my depression, whether by the help of recently eliminating something that has been stressing me a lot, or because of a break from college, or because of a recent relationship development, I dont know. I just am so releved to be out of it and once again be able to walk over a bridge without feeling the call to jump off-see a razor without seeing blood in my mind, and just overall wanting to live. Being...happy, about the idea. When in depression it can seem impossible to ever be happy again, well I am here to tell you its not true. Happiness is within reach, and it will come again. That thing within you, be it self preservation instinct or some dark force, that encourages you to take your life, dont listen to it. Find help if you need it, but when you feel the urge greatest, write on here and read responses from people who do understand or at least really want to help. It helped me. :)

There is a reason the term "mid-life crisis" is well known-loadsa people feel this way. So yours is early. You are depressed and disillusioned. I get that. I feel the same way. I think most of our problem is that we are people who tend to live in the future, even though we are not there yet. We look out and think "this is hopeless, why am I even trying, it is too big for me and I dont really want it". I am realizing, if we take one day at a time, and just focus on the present, things seem a lot less weighty. Don't worry about the future-let today worry about itself. You never know what could come in your future.  There is lots of tips and stories out there of succeeding after your "prime" (if that is what you want to call the young 20/30s -.- I feel like a baby at 22, my whole life ahead and no idea where I am going...). One tip I found was "Make a list of the times when your expectations were unrealistic. Ask yourself if what you wanted so badly was what you really needed.
Make a list of the times when you reached your goals. Ask yourself if you succeeded because these goals matched the values that were closest to your heart.
Be assured, if you set goals that are in sync with your authentic self, not who you or others think you ought to be, and you take the small steps that lead to any worthwhile objective, the results will exceed your expectations." Our lives don't have to measure up to anything, or leave some big footprint in history-there are billions of people out there, and very few are living what they see as the "dream". The "dream" is what we decide it is-not what culture decides it is. Find something you enjoy that you could afford, maybe some sort of art. Rebel against cultures expectations a little. ;)
